Content formats

This is the compatibility record for the current implementation. Planned work is separate from verified behavior. A limited independent keyboard-driving prototype is locally tested; original physics and general gameplay compatibility are not established.

The inventory scope is file_presence_only. Lightweight scene resource inspection remains configuration_and_header_only, with geometry_loaded: false. The separate KN5 reader and local viewer use static_geometry_preview; the viewer reports geometry_loaded: true and whether validated texture resources are available via texture_preview_available. Actual successful texture uploads are counted in the browser inspector. original_shaders remains false; server metadata alone does not prove GPU rendering.

Native KN5 and GPU path

Native configuration and composition

asc-config reads UTF-8 INI/LUT with optional BOM, source lines, case-normalised section/key identifiers, strict duplicate/quote checks, literal backslashes and comments outside quotes. Input is limited to 4 MiB and 100000 nonempty records. LUT x values must strictly increase; values/samples must be finite. Piecewise linear interpolation clamps endpoints and rejects numeric overflow. Native legacy encodings, includes and expressions are unsupported.

asc-scene accepts an explicit models.ini or models_LAYOUT.ini path. It loads static MODEL_n declarations in source order, requires explicit FILE/POSITION/ROTATION, applies translations to geometry/draw centres and ROAD/visible bounds, and rebases indices/materials. Nonzero model rotations fail until the original convention is validated. Absolute, drive-relative, stream, parent-traversal and resolved-outside-root paths are rejected on every host. Invalid static declarations/resources fail the scene rather than silently presenting a partial load. Dynamic sections and unknown keys produce omission warnings.

Composition limits are 256 models, 256 MiB of combined render buffers, 32 MiB of retained model metadata payload (names and property values), 200000 nodes and 100000 materials/textures. One separately bounded KN5 is decoded before the aggregate limit is checked; peak CPU memory can include that in-flight model. Each model keeps its own embedded texture namespace and original file offsets; source (128 MiB), retained texture storage (256 MiB) and upload payload (256 MiB) budgets are shared across the scene. Repeated references currently duplicate model/texture resources. Original shared/cross-model lookup precedence remains unvalidated. Composed summary version 0 marks an aggregate; individual model versions remain in the manifest. No scene model or texture extraction is performed.

The native Rust reader directly consumes one KN5 v5/v6 with no Python runtime. It validates UTF-8, finite numeric fields, boolean fields, affine/composed transforms, material/index references and unexplained trailing data. Structural budgets are 2 GiB per file, 1 MiB per string/32 MiB combined strings, 100000 textures, 10000 materials, 100000 combined properties/mappings each, 200000 nodes and 128 hierarchy depth. Per mesh, at most 2000000 vertices and 12000000 triangle indices are accepted; source geometry and flattened render buffers each have a separate 256 MiB budget. Texture bodies are skipped in place. Skinned geometry is structurally validated but not drawn.

The native renderer draws active visible renderable static indexed meshes with near LOD start at or below zero. World transforms use the same independently tested flat column-major convention as the Python path. UVs survive unchanged. Normals use the inverse-transpose linear transform and normalisation; a singular transform is diagnosed and uses geometric lighting. An upright isometric orthographic camera fits active near-level ROAD geometry when present, otherwise visible geometry. Original indices keep their winding; rendering is double-sided. It writes an sRGB frame and unpads a bounded 256-byte-aligned GPU readback. Library capture dimensions are limited to 1..4096 per axis; the CLI uses 1240 by 900. An explicitly requested new PNG is the only content-derived output file. There is no texture extraction, native driving loop or original shader/physics claim. Native window inspection is a separate command sharing this render pass.

Native diffuse textures and material states

Native structural inspection retains embedded texture ranges without reading their payloads. Rendering resolves exactly one txDiffuse mapping per used material to exactly one active embedded name, compared without ASCII case. Duplicate names/references, inactive entries, malformed DDS, I/O and budget failures are diagnosed and use per-material diagnostic colours. Resource successes and failures are cached by descriptor and colour/data role. The input file remains unchanged. External skin textures are not loaded.

The Rust decoder supports BC1/2/3 and mask-defined 8/16/24/32-bit luminance or 16/24/32-bit RGB, with explicit alpha masks and validated pitch. Dimensions are at most 8192 per axis and 16777216 pixels. Scene budgets are 128 MiB source bytes, 256 MiB retained CPU texture storage and 256 MiB GPU upload payload. BC blocks count at their encoded size; software-decoded pixels count at full RGBA mip size. Limits are checked before allocation/upload. GPU payload counters exclude driver alignment/overhead and the small diagnostic fallback texture; they are not total VRAM measurements. Required masks must be contiguous, in range and nonoverlapping. Cube/volume/DX10/BC4-7/premultiplied variants remain unsupported. The implementation follows the primary DDS layout guide and block compression description, with original decoder code and fixtures.

Authored compressed and raw mip chains are retained. Raw lower levels accept exact tightly packed or exact DWORD-aligned storage; other/ambiguous layouts fail rather than being guessed. Raw base-only textures receive a generated chain using independent linear-sRGB colour/straight-alpha box averaging, including odd edges. This is approximate generated filtering, not original-game parity. The CLI retains validated BC1/2/3 DDS blocks when base dimensions are block-aligned, requests TEXTURE_COMPRESSION_BC only if the selected adapter supports it, and uploads authored levels as BC1/2/3 sRGB. Small mip tails use physical block extents and block-row pitches. Raw and unaligned images use RGBA8 sRGB. Without the device feature, retained BC sources decode one at a time within the remaining upload budget; excess resources use diagnostic colours. Use --rgba-textures to disable the feature and exercise that fallback. Repeat addressing, trilinear filtering and linear alpha remain in use. Per-resource metadata decoded_bytes describes the potential RGBA chain size, not an allocation for retained BC data. Explicit library load_textures/load_track_textures remain CPU RGBA readers; prepare_textures/prepare_track_textures select the encoded-capable path. Feature negotiation follows the wgpu compression feature contract. Full original shader/material behavior remains unimplemented; a reconstructed multilayer base-colour path is described below.

Material preview uses the recorded alpha-test flag or blend mode 2 for a 0.5 cutoff, blend mode 1 for straight-alpha blending, and ignores texture alpha on opaque draws. The alpha property is clamped to 0..1 and ksDiffuse to 0..2 for basic directional lighting. Depth mode 0 uses less-or-equal and writes depth; mode 1 is read-only with a small negative constant/slope bias; mode 2 is always-pass/read-only. Unknown blend/depth values use an opaque depth-writing fallback with a structural diagnostic. Opaque groups precede transparent draws; transparent meshes use stable back-to-front camera-depth sorting of mesh centres. This is approximate mesh sorting rather than per-pixel transparency.

--diagnostic skips texture loading while retaining material-state preview. Rendering reports native_static_diffuse_preview or native_static_material_diagnostics, actual uploaded textures, textured/cutout/blended draw counts, and resource diagnostics. Multilayer base colour is reconstructed for the three listed variants. Original normal/Fresnel/specular lighting, alpha-to-coverage, shadows and full colour-space behavior remain unvalidated. Grass receives detail colour but can still show stippled/coplanar artifacts; a textured frame is not evidence of original visual parity.

Native multilayer base colour

The KN5 reader retains all ten floats of every named shader property and every sampler name, slot and resource reference. materials SCENE prints this metadata without a GPU. The implemented colour path recognises exactly ksMultilayer, ksMultilayer_objsp and ksMultilayer_fresnel_nm. Other shader families retain the existing diffuse preview.

The independently implemented base-colour equation is D * magicMult * (M.r * R + M.g * G + M.b * B + M.a * A), applied componentwise to RGB. D is txDiffuse at source UV, M is txMask at source UV, and R/G/B/A are the four detail samples. Weights are not normalised; mask alpha is a fourth detail weight rather than surface opacity. The original multilayer alpha/specular product is not used by the current approximate lighting path.

For ksMultilayer and its fresnel_nm variant, detail coordinates use transformed world XZ: scalar multR/G/B applies to both axes, while multA uses its float2 values. The objsp variant uses source UV multiplied by four float2 scales. These conventions and colour arithmetic were checked against the local SDK descriptions and installed runtime vertex/pixel shader metadata/arithmetic. The runtime pixel shader SHA256 identifiers begin 5b3df3e0548064fc (ksMultilayer), 38366d9431c27ab5 (fresnel_nm) and 38d1d0b3079ede8e (objsp). SDK/runtime shader binaries and local disassemblies are not distributed.

The preview samples colour maps through sRGB views and masks through linear views. Generated raw-mask mips average data channels without sRGB conversion. Exact original sampler/colour-space state, lighting, normals, Fresnel, specular, fog and shadows are not reproduced or image-validated. This is a reconstructed base-colour path with approximate shading, not an original shader execution or 1:1 visual claim.

All five auxiliary samplers must resolve uniquely within the source model, and required property records must exist. Selected scale/gain values must be finite and within +/-10000. Invalid/missing/ambiguous input or a failed GPU resource produces a named diagnostic and diffuse-only fallback. Colour/data roles have separate cache entries so raw mask mip generation cannot alter colour mips. Primary diffuse resources are queued before optional layers within each model, and GPU upload prioritises diffuse references across the scene, preserving basic preview coverage under the RGBA budget. Retained resources and upload payload stay within shared budgets. Diagnostics identify every enabled multilayer material and its incomplete shading scope; multilayer_draws reports actual selected draws. Diagnostic colour mode disables the layered RGB calculation.

Native window and camera

The view command uses winit 0.30 and wgpu 30 to present a persistent GPU scene on an SDR RGBA8/BGRA8 surface. It selects an sRGB view format and converts BGRA readback to canonical RGBA before PNG encoding. Geometry, texture and material resources survive camera changes and ordinary resize. A bounded orbit camera supports perspective/orthographic projection, pan, zoom and near-top view. Mouse button/cursor state clears on focus loss, cursor exit and resize. The app waits when idle and skips zero-size/occluded views.

Window and offscreen paths share shader/pipeline preparation, scene drawing and aligned readback. Window draws re-sort transparency using current camera direction. T changes diffuse RGB without removing loaded alpha cutouts; report diffuse_enabled/textured_draws describe the current RGB mode. The initial client is 1240 by 900 physical pixels and size is bounded to 4096 per axis. Optional --capture NEW.png saves the first actual surface frame; --captures DIR enables F12 snapshots. Overwrite refusal is retained. Driver surface COPY_SRC support is required only for these captures and the explicit window test.

Outdated/suboptimal surfaces are reconfigured and lost surfaces have at most three recreation attempts. Timeouts have bounded redraw attempts before waiting for further interaction. Unsupported SDR formats, validation errors and capture failures remain explicit. These paths are implemented, not a claim of tested monitor/adapter migration, OS suspend/minimise behavior, mobile support, HDR, device-loss recovery or original game UI compatibility. Native vehicle simulation/FFB remain unimplemented.

INI subset

  • UTF-8 with optional BOM by default; legacy encodings require an explicit selection.
  • Section headers and keys are normalized to uppercase; values remain strings.
  • Keys are split from values at the first equals sign. Empty values are supported.
  • Blank lines and full-line semicolon, hash, or double-slash comments are ignored.
  • Semicolons begin inline comments outside double-quoted values.
  • Whole values may be double-quoted. Backslashes remain literal, without escape processing.
  • Duplicate sections and duplicate keys, including case variants, are errors rather than silently merged values.
  • Keys before a section, malformed headers, bare lines, and malformed quotes are errors.

This strict subset deliberately rejects ambiguous input. It does not claim the original game's complete parser behavior. Section and key source lines are retained in the Python API and diagnostics.

LUT subset

Rows contain exactly two finite numeric values separated by a vertical bar. The following is an original example:

0|10
10|30

The x coordinates must be strictly increasing. Duplicate or descending coordinates, empty tables, extra columns, NaN, and infinity are errors. Scientific notation and a single-point constant table are supported. Comments follow the same rules as the INI reader.

Sampling uses piecewise linear interpolation. The example returns 20 at x=5. Samples outside the domain return the nearest endpoint value. This interpolation policy belongs to openASC's current reader; equivalence to every original game subsystem is not claimed. Extreme numeric ranges that cannot be interpolated reliably are diagnosed.

Static track configuration

The scene inspector selects content/tracks/TRACK/models.ini, or models_LAYOUT.ini when a layout is provided. It requires explicit file, position, and rotation fields in each numbered MODEL section.

Model paths may use forward or backslashes, but must resolve within the selected track folder. Absolute paths, Windows drive-relative paths, parent escapes, and resolved links outside that root are rejected. Vectors require three finite numbers. Values are recorded without interpreting rotation units or applying transforms yet.

Unknown sections and model keys are warnings. Missing resources, invalid transforms, and unsupported KN5 headers are errors. Errors in one model do not suppress diagnostics for the other model declarations. If no model passes inspection, the report also includes no_models.

KN5 headers and static geometry

Local observations confirm the six-byte sc6969 signature followed by a little-endian 32-bit version. Version 6 includes another 32-bit header field. The lightweight scene inspector accepts versions 5 and 6, checks header length, and records file size. It does not validate the remaining structure; a header-only fixture can pass that limited inspection. The separate KN5 reader parses the supported remaining structure and rejects unexplained trailing bytes.

The binary reader handles length-prefixed UTF-8 names, embedded texture descriptors and payload skipping, material properties and sampler mappings, transform nodes, and static triangle meshes. Static vertices contain position, normal, UV, and tangent fields in 44 bytes; indices are 16-bit. Material references and index ranges are checked. Skinned node records are consumed to preserve stream alignment, but their geometry is explicitly omitted from the preview.

The renderer applies node hierarchy transforms and model translations, and samples supported embedded txDiffuse textures with basic lighting. It uses a fixed 0.5 cutoff for alpha-tested/alpha-to-coverage materials, approximate mesh-sorted straight-alpha blending, recorded depth modes, and a small read-only overlay bias. Geometry remains double-sided. Original shader behavior, multilayer/detail/normal maps, shadows, and exact distance-based LOD are not reproduced. Hidden/inactive/non-renderable/empty and later-LOD meshes are omitted with a diagnostic. Nonzero model-level rotations are diagnosed and skipped rather than assigned an unverified Euler convention.

Malformed signatures, versions, truncated fields, invalid flags, unknown node types, invalid indices/material references, nonfinite geometry, non-affine transforms, and numeric overflow produce errors with byte offsets. The reader limits files to 2 GiB, total geometry to 256 MiB, combined string bytes to 32 MiB, nodes to 200000, and hierarchy depth to 128. The assembled local preview additionally limits geometry to 384 MiB. These are current implementation limits, not original engine limits.

Primary implementation references used to check field layouts are AcTools Kn5Basic and kn5-converter. The openASC parser, bounds calculations, diagnostics, renderer, and fixtures are independently written. No source files from these tools are bundled.

Embedded DDS preview

The KN5 importer records texture offsets without extracting payloads. The local viewer resolves a unique active embedded txDiffuse reference for each material, case-insensitively within that model. External texture files and ambiguous embedded names are not guessed. Unsupported or missing resources fall back to diagnostic material colours with warnings.

The supported legacy DDS subset includes DXT1/BC1, DXT3/BC2, DXT5/BC3, mask-defined RGB at 16/24/32 bits, and luminance at 8/16/24/32 bits with optional alpha. Channel masks must be contiguous, in range, and nonoverlapping. The reader validates dimensions, surface kind, declared compressed mip-chain lengths, and uncompressed base row pitch. A declared linear size is not treated as raw row pitch. Cube/volume resources, DX10 headers, BC4-7, premultiplied DXT2/4, and other formats are explicitly unsupported.

Compressed authored mip chains are preserved for upload. Raw textures use their validated base image and GPU-generated mipmaps; lower raw authored mips are not interpreted or validated. The upload payload contains only the retained subset, not a guaranteed complete DDS export. UVs and image row order are passed through without an additional flip.

WebGL uses S3TC when available and compatible with mip dimensions. Otherwise, original JavaScript decodes BC1/2/3 or raw pixels to RGBA. Compressed upload failure also attempts the bounded software path. Alpha indices, endpoint interpolation, cropped blocks, channel masks, padded row order, and both BC3 interpolation branches have original pixel tests. Software rounding may differ slightly from a GPU implementation.

DDS limits are 8192 pixels per axis, 16777216 base pixels, and 128 MiB per embedded source. Per-scene retained texture data is capped at 128 MiB, with a 256 MiB RGBA mip budget covering the software path. These are preview limits. A failed GPU upload is reported in the browser, and never counted as a successful upload.

Opaque materials ignore texture alpha. Material transparency uses the recorded opaque/alpha-blend states; alpha-to-coverage uses a cutoff approximation. Depth modes map to normal, read-only, and disabled depth tests. Mesh-centre sorting does not solve intersecting transparent geometry. Grass and other multilayer materials can look white or otherwise incorrect when only their base map is shown. No shader or material parity is claimed.

The independent DDS implementation was checked against the primary Microsoft documentation for DDS headers, pixel formats, and block compression. Recorded state names are cross-checked against AcTools blend and depth definitions. No third-party decoder source is bundled.

Surface definitions and ground support

The ground command reports static_ground_query, independently of the rendering preview. It reads system/data/surfaces.ini and then content/tracks/TRACK/data/surfaces.ini. With a layout, the second path is content/tracks/TRACK/LAYOUT/data/surfaces.ini; the base track file is not used as a fallback. Same-KEY track definitions completely replace system definitions. Missing files produce warnings; no available definitions produce an error. An invalid selected file fails loading instead of silently falling back to a system coefficient. This explicit policy is tested, but equivalence to every original loader precedence rule is not established.

Numbered SURFACE sections require KEY, FRICTION, DAMPING, IS_VALID_TRACK and IS_PITLANE. Keys are normalized to uppercase ASCII identifiers. Friction and damping must be finite and nonnegative; the two flags must be 0 or 1. Other known numeric fields are validated as finite metadata. Sound/FFB references and unknown fields are retained without execution; unknown fields/sections produce warnings. Duplicate keys within one file are errors, with the original source and line preserved.

The supported physical naming subset requires a leading decimal integer greater than zero, including zero-padded names such as 01ROAD. Exactly one configured surface KEY must prefix the remaining mesh name. Missing or ambiguous matches are diagnosed and omitted; no guessed friction is substituted. Names containing WALL are omitted from the vertical probe and collected into a separate static collider when requested by ground --walls or drive. This conservative prefix policy is openASC behavior, rather than a claim to reproduce all original name matching. Naming and default-surface locations were cross-checked against the author-maintained track construction guide and the local installation.

Active supported physical meshes are included even when hidden or non-renderable. Inactive, empty, later-LOD and skinned geometry are omitted. Node transforms and model translations are applied; nonzero model rotations are diagnosed and omitted. The loader retains up to 1000000 input triangles across models, including subsequently discarded degenerate faces, with world coordinates bounded to +/-10000000 metres. These are current openASC limits. The geometric query builds a median BVH and retains double-precision transformed positions. Faces whose XZ projected area is at most 1e-12 * max(1, projected edge length product) are excluded as vertical or degenerate.

A probe accepts a finite X/Y/Z origin and nonnegative finite maximum distance, within the same 10000000 metre range. It returns the nearest double-sided triangle below the origin, its geometric height, upward unit normal, mesh/model identity and source surface definition. Multiple road levels are queried relative to the origin, so a bridge above it is not chosen. Shared edges are included with numeric tolerance; equal-height ties use original triangle order. Distance/height comparisons use a 0.0000001 metre tolerance, and barycentric comparisons use a 0.000000001 tolerance. A miss returns null. Invalid query input is an error; a miss alone is not.

This query is geometric preparation for wheel support. It does not implement rigid-body collision, walls, suspension, tyre forces, procedural sinusoidal bumps, surface sound, dirt accumulation, penalties or FFB. Recorded friction/damping and validity/pit flags are metadata for later systems. The rendering viewer's ROAD-name focus button remains a separate bounding-box heuristic.

Native rigid instances and session preview

The native scene renderer supports one default root plus up to 255 nonoverlapping draw-range roots. A root is a finite rigid pose: translation within +/-10000000 metres and a unit quaternion with squared norm within 1e-6 before normalization. Source bases require unit/orthogonal axes and right-handed determinant within 1e-6. Scale/skew/reflection is not inferred or repaired beyond numeric quaternion normalization. Transformed bounds and draw centres are validated before a pose change is committed.

Geometry and material resources remain persistent. Each root owns a 128-byte view/model uniform and bind group. WGSL transforms vertex positions and normals to world space, preserving UVs and applying world-position material operations there. Updated world draw centres participate in the existing global transparent sort across all roots; no separate car pass breaks depth/blending order. Updating a root changes its pose/centres and per-frame uniform data, without rebuilding vertex/index/texture resources. One pose per root is encoded per submitted frame. This is rigid grouping of draws, not skeletal animation or shared-geometry crowd instancing.

The preview application loads explicit static track sources and one selected car model, rebases its indices/materials, preserves per-source embedded-texture namespaces, and gives only the car draw range its root. It retains the existing combined budgets: 256 MiB geometry, 32 MiB metadata payload, 200000 nodes, 100000 materials/textures and 256 model sources. The existing shared prepared-texture/upload budgets also apply. A source-relative car model path remains confined to its car folder. Car/track files and external skin files are not extracted or distributed.

The inspection transform is marker position/basis composed with graphics translation and local X pitch (degrees converted to radians). It is not a chassis equilibrium or an assignment of marker height to a validated physical centre of mass. The marker report's errors remain visible, while usable selected poses can still be rendered. Native vehicle forces/input, wheel animation, external skin resolution and original paint/glass/reflection/shadow behavior are not implemented by this preview.

Two new GPU-independent root tests cover graphics/body composition, transformed bounds and invalid poses. Two application fixtures cover rebasing, independent same-named textures, unbaked local car geometry and selected-marker/resource failures. Two explicit GPU tests compare root-transformed geometry/normals against a baked reference and move a persistent transparent root across another mesh, checking changed world sorting without resource reload. The additional window fixture verifies two roots, camera/resize/readback and texture toggling under the real native presenter. Including the separate telemetry tool, the current Windows suite has 267 GPU-independent tests, eleven explicit offscreen GPU tests and six explicit window tests. Actual mouse/keyboard gestures remain outside the independent UI verification record.

Local Windows/Vulkan/RTX 2080 BMW M3 E30/Drift inspection renders 1268567 triangles: 1150970 track triangles and 117597 car triangles, in 254 track/166 car draws. Two roots share 72 uploaded textures, 50 compressed resources and 116351768 uploaded payload bytes. Both offscreen capture and five-frame window presentation with four readbacks pass. The car is recognisable in the flattened progress capture, with approximate white paint, glass/lighting artifacts and an unsolved marker-plane placement. It reports driving false, simulation_ready false and the pre-existing duplicate AC_START_3 diagnostic. This is native session inspection, not an original-game image or a native controlled drive.

Native spring links and suspension records

asc-vehicle::suspension separately reads explicit STRUT/DWB source records through the existing whole-source ACD/unpacked loader. HEADER versions 1/2 are accepted. Each axle requires its common lower/steering hardpoints plus STRUT_CAR/STRUT_TYRE or DWB upper hardpoints, with original names and unmodified finite coordinates. It records wheelbase, front fraction, track, BASEY, signed ROD_LENGTH and HUB_MASS, fourteen original numeric spring/damper/stop/toe/camber fields and optional complete ARB FRONT/REAR values. All consumed fields retain source/line provenance. Missing explicit fields, unsupported types and malformed values fail; unknown fields/extra sections warn rather than being simulated. No implicit ARB stiffness is invented when the section is absent.

Reader bounds are wheelbase/track within (0,100] metres, front fraction strictly within (0,1), BASEY/rod within +/-100 metres, positive recorded hub mass up to 1e6 kg and hardpoint components within +/-1000 metres. Rate/threshold/stop source numbers must be finite and nonnegative up to 1e12; signed toe/camber numbers are bounded by +/-1e6. Zero rates are retained. These are input limits, not original-engine compatibility limits. Source *_THRESHOLD numbers remain raw records; exact units/interpolation and hub-mass assignment are not established by loading them. The report explicitly sets simulation_ready false. There is no automatic conversion from these records to the independent force link.

The native SpringLink uses body-local attachment points on two rigid bodies. Along the world endpoint axis, extension is length minus explicit rest length and extension rate is relative point velocity projected on that axis, including angular point velocity. Elastic tension is k times extension. The separate compression/rebound damper branches use nonnegative slow/fast slopes and a continuous knee: slow*min(speed,knee)+fast*max(speed-knee,0), with the extension-rate sign restored. A zero knee uses the fast slope at nonzero speed. This is an independently chosen passive constitutive law; original AC damper/progressive/stop behavior is not claimed. Linear spring and viscous-damper relations are documented in the primary spring and damper references; no external implementation is bundled.

The link returns equal/opposite forces and attachment torques, elastic energy k*extension^2/2 and nonnegative instantaneous damping power. Numeric bounds are slopes 0..1e9 N s/m, knees 0..1000 m/s, extension-rate magnitude at most 1e6 m/s, local attachment components within +/-10000 metres, rest length 1e-6..10000 metres and stiffness 0..1e9 N/m. Endpoint separation must be 1e-9..10000 metres; coincident endpoints are rejected instead of assigning an arbitrary axis. The existing body/wrench bounds also apply.

step_springs validates at most 4096 bodies/16384 links, distinct valid endpoint indices and exactly one explicit external wrench per body. It sums all links at the current state, predicts all half-step states, resamples at their common midpoint, then advances and commits every body once. Any topology/load/body error leaves all input bodies unchanged. step_pair wraps the same graph path for an isolated pair. Duration is 2e-6..1/30 seconds so both the predictor and final body steps satisfy the kernel limits. External wrenches remain constant through the step. This is explicit second-order force coupling; no unilateral contact, DWB/STRUT constraints or universal energy/stability guarantee is supplied.

Seven original force-link tests cover both damper knees/signs/passivity, zero rates, endpoint/world transforms, rotational point velocity, action/reaction and moment balance, mechanical power balance, analytic damped-oscillator convergence, damped/undamped energy, whole-pair failure rollback, shared-body graph stepping and invalid topology/numerics. The oscillator's extension error is below 1e-5 m at 480 Hz and reduces by a factor below 0.35 when rate doubles. The undamped five-second 240 Hz fixture bounds relative energy error below 1e-3; the damped case decreases energy within its fixture tolerance. A shared-body three-body fixture checks a common gravitational fall and symmetric internal oscillation, preventing repeated integration of a shared body. The spring_pair executable repeats an original analytic check in Windows/Linux CI and reports original_suspension_validated false, simulation_ready false.

Four source-reader tests cover packed/unpacked records, source locations, whole-source precedence, malformed/missing fields, unsupported types, signed rod/zero rates, optional ARB and unknown sections. The parity tool compares original packed/unpacked fixtures and optionally local source values/provenance; the local BMW M3 E30 matches all 58 consumed fields, with STRUT front/DWB rear. No source files are exported. The spring/source-record milestone passed 102 GPU-independent tests; existing explicit GPU/window checks remain separate. This milestone prepares force inputs and a coupled mechanical element; native car equilibrium, tyre forces, contact constraints and controlled driving remain incomplete.

Native rigid body and fixed step path

asc-physics is an unconstrained 3D kernel. Its physical state is centre-of-mass position, a unit body-to-world quaternion [x,y,z,w], and world linear/angular momenta. It derives velocity from mass and angular velocity from the rotated inverse body tensor. Force changes linear momentum, torque changes angular momentum, and a force at a point contributes its lever-arm cross product about the centre of mass. These mathematical relationships follow David Baraff's unconstrained rigid-body notes; openASC's implementation, numeric policy and tests are independently written. No course source code is included.

The supplied inertia tensor uses row order in kg m2 about the centre of mass. The constructor accepts mass in 1e-9..1e12 kg and tensor scale in 1e-12..1e18 kg m2. It checks finite values, symmetry within a scale-relative 1e-12, scaled Cholesky pivots above 1e-12 and a Frobenius condition estimate at most 1e12. Small symmetric rounding differences are averaged. Physical realizability is checked through Cholesky of the mass covariance (half the inertia trace times identity minus the inertia tensor), with a scaled 1e-12 diagonal tolerance. Positive-definite tensors that violate principal-moment triangle inequalities are rejected, including a rotated near-degenerate regression case.

The independent step holds one explicit world wrench constant for its duration, updates momenta, uses midpoint translation and an explicit Lie-midpoint quaternion rotation. This is a second-order unconstrained integration choice, not a recovered Assetto Corsa integrator. Torque-free world angular momentum remains constant; the changing world inertia supplies gyroscopic motion. Forces are explicit per step and do not accumulate across calls. No gravity, damping, tyre friction or ground constraints are silently inserted. Rotational energy is approximate: long-term conservation is not guaranteed.

Step duration is limited to 1e-6..1/30 seconds and rotation to 0.25 radians per step. Position components stay within +/-10000000 metres, COM velocity components within +/-1000000 m/s, angular velocity components within +/-100000 rad/s, and supplied force/torque or impulse components within +/-1e18 in their SI units. Initial quaternion squared norm must be within 1e-6 of one before normalization. Candidates are validated before body/load state is committed; invalid steps, impulses and load sums return errors without partial mutation. Forces at world points and body-local points have separate APIs.

FixedClock accepts 30..10000 Hz and a 1..10000 per-advance work budget. Nanoseconds are multiplied by the rate into integer credits, with one billion credits per tick; the solver duration remains exactly the floating-point value 1/rate. Backlog is retained, with no interpolation alpha while whole steps remain. Each successful callback commits one tick. A failed callback retains that tick's credit and index while earlier successful ticks stay committed; callbacks must commit their own external state transactionally. Time/counter overflow is rejected. The same tick/load sequence is independent of presentation-frame grouping.

The session bridge requires explicit mass properties and centre-of-mass position. It copies the spawn orientation only if its basis is rigid within 1e-6 before quaternion conversion. It does not infer a physical tensor from car.ini INERTIA dimensions or a chassis equilibrium from the marker plane. The tighter check rejects skew, reflections and nonfinite public marker data. This kernel does not make native vehicle driving available.

Twelve original physics tests cover full/non-diagonal tensors, rotated moments, invalid/physically impossible inertia, constant force/torque analytic solutions, symmetric-top closed-form convergence, asymmetric torque-free motion, lever arms, force couples, impulses, point velocity, rejected-state atomicity, frame grouping, fractional nanosecond credits, backlog and callback retry. Two session tests cover explicit COM/basis integration and invalid bases. The rigid-body milestone passed 91 GPU-independent tests; explicit GPU/window checks remain separate. The symmetric-top case verifies error reduction below 0.35 when doubling rate, with final orientation error below 1e-4 rad at 480 Hz. The asymmetric case retains world momenta exactly and bounds relative rotational kinetic-energy drift below 1e-4 over ten seconds at 240 Hz. These tolerances describe these original fixtures, not arbitrary vehicle stability or original simulator fidelity.

The free_body example is run in Windows/Linux CI. It checks 120 committed ticks after an eight-step initial work budget, final position (0.5,5.095,0.75) within 1e-10 m and final angular momentum (1,0.5,0.25) within 1e-12 kg m2/s. It exports original synthetic state only and explicitly reports original_physics_validated false, simulation_ready false.

Native spawn and placement path

The native node-only KN5 mode validates supported v5/v6 structure, indices, fields and trailing bytes without retaining mesh buffers. It returns preorder node records with original kind/name, parent index, inherited active state and composed double-precision world matrix. Rendering and physical mesh modes share the same structural parser. The existing KN5 limits still apply: 2 GiB input, 256 MiB source geometry, 32 MiB combined strings, 200000 nodes and depth 128. Spawn loading also limits combined scene nodes to 200000, canonical identities to 4096, and retained spawn/diagnostic payload to 32 MiB.

asc-scene::spawns supports exact canonical AC_PIT_N, AC_START_N and AC_HOTLAP_START_0 names. A named transform and its same-named directly attached static/skinned cube share one identity only when their source world matrices match. Separate duplicate nodes/models do not become one marker merely because their positions match; the identity is excluded and diagnosed. Identity tracking occurs before basis validation, so an invalid first marker cannot hide a later duplicate. Inactive ancestry excludes markers. Standalone skinned markers and noncanonical names produce warnings. Model declarations use the same confined static sources as rendering/ground; invalid files or nonzero model rotations fail instead of yielding a silent partial scene.

Spawn bases require finite affine matrices, unit-length and mutually orthogonal axes within 1e-3, right-handed determinant within 1e-3 of one, up-Y greater than 0.5 and translation within +/-10000000 metres. The affine tolerance is 1e-5. No skew/scale/handedness repair or Euler conversion is applied. The retained convention is local +X left, +Y up, +Z forward, with explicit model translation applied to the source node world transform.

asc-session::place combines typed vehicle configuration, one unambiguous selected spawn and native static ground. The four footprint origins use spawn position + left times wheel X + forward times wheel Z; vertical queries use a 20-metre limit. BASEY, tyre radius, graphics offsets and suspension equilibrium are not interpreted as chassis placement. Contacts retain model/mesh, triangle, position, distance, upward normal and surface metadata. Missing support is an error; global spawn errors remain visible even when the selected footprint has four hits. Native spawns/place commands return a nonzero status when their printed report has errors. This is contact preparation with simulation_ready false, not a native driving session.

Eight native spawn/session tests cover preorder parents, hidden/static/skinned marker aliases, inherited activity, rotated bases/model translations, true duplicates across nodes/models, canonical names, invalid bases, limits, fatal source errors, four-wheel support/misses, selected ambiguity and source-content preservation. CI compares four original placement cases (packed/unpacked vehicles, rotated footprint, unrelated duplicate, missing support), process statuses and ambiguous selection rejection against the research implementation. The spawn/placement milestone passed 77 GPU-independent tests; explicit GPU/window tests remain separate.

Local native BMW M3 E30/Drift preparation agrees with the Python path for all 35 usable marker transforms and the selected AC_PIT_0 basis, wheel footprint origins, support triangle identities, positions, distances, normals and surface metadata (absolute tolerance 1e-7, relative tolerance 1e-10). All four contacts hit ROAD about 0.554 metres below the marker plane. Both reports preserve the duplicate AC_START_3 error and report has_errors true, simulation_ready false. The game content and generated reports remain local. No native equilibrium, tyre force, original handling or driving compatibility is established.

Native static ground path

asc-scene::sources resolves static declarations without loading render geometry; native rendering and ground assembly share its confined model paths, explicit translations, zero-rotation requirement and 256-model limit. The KN5 collision path reads active static meshes with nonzero numeric physical prefixes into double-precision positions independently of visible/renderable flags. It retains near/far LOD metadata; ground assembly omits positive near-LOD meshes with an explicit diagnostic. Skinned meshes are structurally checked and omitted. Texture payloads are skipped without decoding or extraction. Render geometry remains float32 and its existing selection policy is unchanged.

asc-ground consumes explicit surface file paths in order. Later files replace complete same-KEY definitions. Required fields are KEY, FRICTION, DAMPING, IS_VALID_TRACK and IS_PITLANE. Coefficients must be finite and nonnegative; flags are 0 or 1. Other known numeric fields are checked for finiteness and retained. Uninterpreted fields and unsupported sections produce diagnostics. Duplicate keys within one file, invalid overrides, missing explicitly requested files and ambiguous mesh prefix matches are not silently accepted. WALL meshes are separate from the vertical support query. At most 16 surface files and 4096 merged surface keys are accepted.

The ground builder limits selected input to one million triangles, combined source nodes to 200000, retained mesh/surface/diagnostic metadata payload to 32 MiB, and coordinates to +/-10000000 metres. Each KN5 reader retains its 256 MiB source geometry budget; collision buffers additionally have a 256 MiB retained payload budget. Projected degenerate/vertical triangles are counted and omitted. A median BVH accelerates double-sided downward queries with inclusive shared edges, upward unit geometric normals and deterministic source-order selection at equal heights. Probe distances must be finite and within 0..10000000 metres. This is a static vertical query, not arbitrary raycasting or a physical contact solver. Coefficients are metadata and the report explicitly states simulation_ready false.

The static-ground milestone passed 69 GPU-independent tests; nine explicit offscreen GPU tests and four window tests remain separate. Eight original native ground tests cover hidden physical geometry, active ancestry, double-precision transform retention, ramps of either winding, shared edges, bridges, query limits, analytic-plane checks across 576 triangles/two models, complete surface precedence, malformed definitions, diagnostics/empty geometry, positive near-LOD omission, translated-coordinate and triangle limits, and repeated metadata budgets. Native/Python CI compares original v5/v6 physical fixtures, model translations, complete mesh/surface metadata, hits and misses without source writes. Warning text/order is not compared.

Local Drift assembled 54522 supported triangles from 56 meshes; Magione assembled 365267 from 212 meshes. On each track, 1000 fixed-seed centroid probes plus two misses agreed with the Python research path for selected triangle, model/mesh, position, distance, upward normal and surface metadata (absolute numeric tolerance 1e-7, relative tolerance 1e-10). Source files and generated reports remain local. Agreement between these two implementations does not prove original Assetto Corsa physics or universal track compatibility.

Native vehicle and ACD path

asc-acd and asc-vehicle now implement the ordinary archive/configuration subset directly in Rust, without a Python process or GPU. The car command accepts a car directory, selects packed or unpacked input as a whole, and returns typed configuration with field provenance. The acd command exposes an immutable validated record index, not decoded entry export.

The archive reader uses the existing bounded record contract: 64 MiB source, 4096 entries, 1..255-byte flat ASCII names, 8 MiB per decoded entry and 16 MiB combined declared decoded bytes. It preserves the optional legacy extra word without assigning semantics, resets the decimal folder key at every record, and reports structural failures with source/byte offsets. Independent fixed key/encoded-record vectors cover short identifiers, case normalisation and signed 32-bit wrapping. Archives are not authenticated; other protected variants are unsupported. No extraction/writing API is supplied.

Native car identifiers are 1..128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. Selected unpacked files are case-insensitive by name, with ambiguous duplicates rejected. Auto chooses an existing data directory, warns if both sources exist, and never fills missing files from data.acd. Explicit packed selection does not open an unselected data directory. Selected model/data references must remain within their respective roots after canonicalisation. The reader assumes stable local content during loading; confinement is not a race-proof OS sandbox.

The loaded-data cache is limited to 16 MiB with an 8 MiB per-file bound; the INI/LUT parser additionally applies its 4 MiB text and 100000-record bounds. Native text is UTF-8 with an optional BOM. Supported header versions are car 1, suspensions 1/2, tyres 7/10, engine 1, drivetrain 1/2/3 and brakes 1. The loader requires finite values, positive mass/dimensions/forward and final ratios, a negative reverse ratio, a strictly interior CG fraction, valid gear/compound ranges, and a strictly increasing torque LUT spanning idle through limiter.

Outputs include source-valued mass and inertia dimensions, graphics offsets, steering, axle/tyre dimensions, engine inertia/base torque LUT, traction/gears, brakes, geometric wheel offsets, selected compound and first-model header. Inertia dimensions are not a tensor; the model is checked only for a supported header. Turbo and uninterpreted fields produce warnings. simulation_ready remains false: native suspension/tyre/drivetrain behavior, fuel, coast, aero, electronics, FFB and audio are not implemented by this configuration reader. Agreement with Python proves reader contracts rather than original-game behavior.

The vehicle/ACD milestone had 61 GPU-independent tests, nine explicit offscreen GPU tests and four window tests. New cases cover fixed archive vectors, every truncated prefix, malformed names/lengths, budgets, packed/unpacked parity, explicit whole-source precedence, field provenance, tyre compounds, numeric/LUT domains, confined paths, UTF-8 failures and incomplete-feature warnings. Unix-specific fixtures additionally exercise symlink escapes and case-ambiguous unpacked names. The Python/native contract tool now checks five synthetic vehicle configurations, including ignored neighboring filenames, rejects mixed-source loading and invalid fields, and optionally compares local car directories through --car.

Unpacked directory indexing

Rust and Python now bound the selected unpacked directory to 4096 immediate entries before sorting or accumulating ignored-name diagnostics. Files and subdirectories both count, including ignored entries. Non-file entries remain unselected. An unrelated file whose name is outside the flat portable ASCII namespace produces car_data_name_ignored and is not added to the resource index; its content is not read. Non-UTF-8 filenames are also excluded by the native index. The files remain untouched.

Explicitly requested names still pass the strict name validator. A conflicted copy never supplies tyres.ini, a missing unpacked resource never falls back to the archive, and case-insensitive collisions between selectable names remain fatal. Packed archive entry-name validation is unchanged; this policy applies to neighboring files in an unpacked filesystem directory, not malformed ACD records.

New original fixtures check invalid-byte conflict copies alongside valid configuration, ignored files remaining unselectable, missing-required-file rejection despite an archive/copy, explicit packed isolation, and the exact 4096-entry boundary with ignored files and subdirectories. Unix additionally checks a non-UTF-8 neighboring filename and case collision. Python has equivalent behavior tests; the cross-reader tool compares ignored-name diagnostic counts as well as typed fields, including a new neighbor-file fixture.

The local SDK Formula K directory now loads without changing its conflict-copy file. Rust/Python vehicle-subset comparison agrees on fields and provenance, including an 18-point torque curve; the suspension comparison checks all 59 consumed fields and source lines. Its front and rear DWB design poses solve at +25/-25 mm respectively in three iterations. These are source-reader and geometric constraint results, not original-game driving or suspension-force validation. Temporary logs and original SDK files remain excluded from Git.

Packed and unpacked vehicle configuration

The car command uses vehicle_configuration_subset, with simulation_ready: false. It selects content/cars/CAR/data/ if present, otherwise data.acd, unless an explicit packed/unpacked source is requested. Selection applies to the complete source, with no per-file fallback. Data references use flat case-insensitive ASCII filenames. Directory entries that collide case-insensitively are rejected, and resolved file links must stay inside the selected data directory. Referenced visual models must stay inside the car directory. Text decoding is UTF-8 with optional BOM by default, or an explicitly selected encoding.

Ordinary ACD records contain little-endian signed lengths, a plain ASCII filename and an encoded payload with one relevant byte per four stored bytes. The optional -1111 prefix and following word are retained; the extra word's semantics and the other three payload bytes are not interpreted. Eight legacy checksums of the lowercase ASCII folder identifier produce the decimal ASCII key; subtraction modulo 256 restarts at each entry. Indexing validates the complete archive structure before any entry is read. Truncated fields, unsafe/duplicate names, invalid counts and budget violations are errors with byte offsets. There is no authenticated integrity check, so a different folder key is not guaranteed to produce a dedicated wrong-key error; downstream text/config validation still applies. Nonstandard/protected variants are not guessed. The reader has no extraction or writing API.

Limits are 64 MiB per archive, 4096 records, 255 filename bytes, 8 MiB per decoded entry and 16 MiB combined declared decoded data. Folder key identifiers support 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. Unpacked selected files use the same per-file and loaded-data budgets. Archive layout and checksum behavior were cross-checked against primary implementations in AcTools AcdReader and AssettoTools ACDEncryption. The bounded index, car source abstraction, diagnostics and tests are original code; no third-party implementation is bundled.

The vehicle subset requires car/engine/brakes version 1, suspensions version 1 or 2, tyres version 7 or 10, and drivetrain version 1, 2 or 3. These version gates admit the documented configuration subset, not complete schema support. Required mass, dimensions, steering ratio/lock, wheelbase, track widths, tyre dimensions, engine inertia, forward/final gear ratios and brake torque must be positive finite values. Front weight fraction is strictly between zero and one; reverse ratio must be negative. Gear count is an integer from 1 to 10. The selected compound is 0–99; its front/rear sections must exist. An absent requested compound never selects another one.

The external power LUT is recorded in RPM/Nm and must contain at least two strictly increasing nonnegative RPM coordinates covering idle through the positive limiter. Limiter must exceed idle in this subset. Turbo sections produce an explicit warning that the base table alone does not describe boosted output. Other fields are counted as uninterpreted per file. Consumed INI field sources/lines are retained. Local SDK comments were used to check units. INERTIA stores dimensions in metres, not a ready-to-use inertia tensor; TOTALMASS records configured mass without simulating fuel. The LOD_0 model reference receives only path/existence/header validation here.

Spawn transforms and placement preflight

The KN5 reader retains each node's name, kind, active state, parent index and composed transform, including non-rendered nodes. Supported marker names are exactly AC_PIT_n, AC_START_n and AC_HOTLAP_START_0 with canonical nonnegative decimal indices. Inactive markers are omitted. A named transform and its same-named directly attached mesh at the identical inherited transform are one marker; separate duplicate markers remain errors even at identical coordinates, and that name is omitted. Noncanonical names, standalone skinned markers and invalid bases are diagnosed. Mesh-only static markers are also accepted.

Marker bases must be finite, orthogonal, unit-length and orientation-preserving within 0.001 tolerance. The source Y axis must have a world-up component greater than 0.5. Position coordinates are limited to +/-10000000 metres. Scaled, skewed, mirrored or upside-down markers are rejected, rather than repaired. Model translation and node hierarchy are applied; unvalidated model-level rotations are diagnosed and omitted. Y-up/Z-forward marker conventions were checked against the author-maintained track construction guide. Positive X identifies the left side in the local BMW wheel nodes, so the supported vehicle footprint uses +X left, +Y up, +Z forward. No Euler conversion is used for these source bases.

For wheelbase L and configured front static weight fraction f, front footprint Z is (1-f)*L and rear footprint Z is -f*L. Left/right offsets are plus/minus half the configured axle track. The preflight applies the selected spawn basis to X/Z offsets and casts downward 20 metres from the marker plane. It returns each geometric hit and the independent all_wheels_supported flag, while catalog/model errors still set has_errors. BASEY and tyre radius are recorded but not used to solve the chassis height, spring preload or static equilibrium. This is not a body-clearance test, rigid-body solver, tyre model or playable drive.

Independent first-drive prototype

drive assembles the car's first supported visual model into the track preview, sharing the existing geometry and texture budgets. It starts a paused Python simulation and a loopback controller session, with scope: first_drive_prototype. The static car/placement inspection commands retain their separate scopes and simulation_ready: false fields; those reports alone do not instantiate a running model.

The model uses four planar wheel-force patches, rather than original Assetto Corsa physics. World coordinates use +X left, +Y up and +Z forward. Each patch velocity includes body translation and yaw velocity at its configured axle/track offset. Front patches rotate by the steering angle, rate-limited to 1.2 rad/s; the maximum angle is configured steering lock divided by steering ratio. Lateral force is an original regularized slip-angle approximation with corner gain 7 per radian, using a minimum 1.5 m/s longitudinal speed in the denominator. Friction circles limit combined patch forces to the configured surface coefficient times the static normal load. Surface friction must be in the finite 0–5 prototype range.

Configured base engine torque is linearly sampled from RPM, multiplied by throttle, selected gear/final ratio and a prototype 0.9 efficiency, then divided across the driven wheels by tyre radius. A simplified rolling coupling clamps RPM to at least idle, representing assisted launch; limiter cuts drive torque. Neutral has no drive force. Braking interprets MAX_TORQUE as total torque split by front share and axle wheels, with rear handbrake torque added separately. This interpretation and assisted launch do not claim original drivetrain equivalence. Generic rolling resistance is 0.015 of normal load, and longitudinal speed-squared drag uses a prototype coefficient of 0.4 N/(m/s)^2. Low-speed braking uses bounded contact impulses to oppose patch motion and grade gravity, without an unconditional friction-free stop.

Newton force/moment sums update XZ translation and yaw with a semi-implicit fixed step of 1/120 second. Yaw inertia uses the box approximation mass * (width^2 + length^2) / 12, interpreting INERTIA as dimensions. Normal load uses configured front weight fraction, divided equally left/right and scaled by contact normal Y. Grade gravity is projected using the weighted contact normal. No dynamic load transfer, engine/wheel inertia, tyre rotational slip, real suspension or six-degree-of-freedom body response is solved. The force/moment structure was checked against primary 3DOF vehicle-model documentation; the implementation, regularization and prototype tuning are original openASC choices.

At each accepted step, four downward probes select static support below the predicted footprint. Chassis Y is the static-load-weighted mean of ground height + tyre radius - BASEY; the weighted geometric normal sets visual pitch/roll, with forward projected onto its plane. This is geometric attachment, not spring equilibrium or wheel/body clearance. Missing support, contact normal Y below 0.5, a vertical step over 0.35 metre, horizontal speed over 150 m/s, yaw rate over 10 rad/s, or numeric/range failure pauses at the last valid position and zeros motion. The drive command separately resolves supported static WALL geometry with the bounded upright body proxy described below. The visual car uses source hierarchy, graphics translation and a local X pitch rotation, with approximate materials; wheel steer/spin and skin textures are not animated/resolved.

Naturally aspirated RWD/FWD vehicles only are admitted. Prototype bounds are mass 50–10000 kg, wheelbase 0.5–10 m, track 0.1–6 m, tyre radius 0.05–2 m, absolute BASEY at most 2 m, steering angle 0.01–0.8 rad, and inertia width/length 0.1–20 m. Base table torque magnitude must not exceed 20000 Nm, limiter 30000 RPM, gear-ratio magnitude 100, final ratio 20, or brake/handbrake torque 100000 Nm. These numerical guards delimit this prototype; they are not original engine limits or a claim that every admitted car is compatible.

The simulation clock is independent of browser redraws and telemetry reads. Catch-up is limited to eight fixed steps per wake; discarded wall-clock backlog increments a visible lag counter. A complete input heartbeat is sent at approximately 20 Hz; expiry after 0.5 second pauses and clears controls. Window blur and tab hiding also request a pause. A local session nonce, strict JSON command fields, monotonically increasing sequence, 2048-byte body limit and same-origin Host/Origin checks constrain the input endpoint. Sequence replay is rejected. Only one controller tab is supported. These local HTTP messages are not multiplayer/network gameplay support.

Static wall and body contact

Driving loads active near-level meshes whose names contain WALL, regardless of render visibility, during the same model read used by the ground loader. The independent ground --walls report also exposes this separate geometry index; vertical probes still ignore wall faces. Model/node transforms and translations follow the existing validated subset. A separate 3D BVH indexes up to 250000 input wall triangles, including subsequently discarded degenerate faces, with coordinates within +/-10000000 metres. Winding is not used to make faces one-sided. Static and moving obstacles without supported WALL naming are not included.

The drive command now requires the selected car's collider.kn5. The reader takes bounds of active indexed static collider vertices after node hierarchy and the same graphics offset/local X pitch convention used by the approximate vehicle renderer. Skinned, empty, flat or out-of-range colliders fail loading; there is no substitution with INERTIA dimensions. Coordinates must remain within +/-20 metres and each box half-extent within 0.01–10 metres. The result is an upright yaw-oriented box enclosing those vertices, rather than the original convex shape. Visual road pitch/roll does not rotate this prototype contact box. Auxiliary ground boxes in colliders.ini, body/ground scraping and deformable/dynamic bodies remain unsupported.

Broad-phase bounds include translation, full corner radius and body height. Narrow-phase separation uses the box face axes, triangle normal and edge cross products. Sweeps follow linear CG translation and the shortest yaw interval between fixed-step poses, with a 0.002 metre contact skin. Corner projections are linear-plus-sinusoidal curves; derivative roots divide them into monotonic intervals. The solver advances to the earliest crossing of a current separating plane, using bounded bisection on those intervals. Interior rotational extrema are included, so endpoint-only tests and near-tangent rotation are not substituted for a continuous query. Existing contacts can slide or separate when an exact swept projection proves the separating plane stays clear. Geometry concept references are the primary dyn4j SAT explanation and Box2D collision documentation; the implementation and fixtures are original openASC code.

Contact generation clips triangles against the skin-expanded box and retains planar manifold ends. A deterministic 12-pass projected impulse solver changes XZ velocity and yaw rate. Restitution is zero; prototype tangential friction is capped at 0.35 times accumulated normal impulse. There is no positional energy bias, damage or claim of original collision tuning. The model can slide along a barrier and reverse away after stopping. Near-simultaneous triangle contacts are grouped within a 0.000001 step fraction; more than 64 manifold points or failure to converge within 80 separating-plane advances is diagnosed.

A fixed step processes at most eight contact events. When that cap is reached, remaining motion is dropped at the last nonpenetrating pose and wall_motion_clamps increments; simulation time still advances by the fixed step. wall_contacts counts contact-resolution events, not distinct crashes, and last_wall_contact identifies the triangle, mesh, point, normal and resolved normal impulse. Spawn overlaps fail startup. A terrain attachment that would put the box inside a wall, an almost vertical response normal, or a numeric/query limit pauses with a diagnostic. Final proxy overlap checks use a 0.000001 metre tolerance. This is bounded planar contact against static triangles, not a complete 3D rigid-body engine or guaranteed contact for all assets.

Local validation record

On 2026-10-18, the native car command loaded the packed local BMW M3 E30 configuration: 1275 kg mass, 2.565 m wheelbase, five forward ratios and a 21-point base torque LUT. Every configuration field, source line, compound selection and model header agreed with the Python reader. Original fixtures additionally agreed for packed/unpacked loading, compound 1 and explicit packed selection, and rejected implicit source mixing and invalid numeric/version inputs. This validates the reader contracts, not original vehicle physics. The native report remains simulation_ready false.

On 2026-10-18, the native Vulkan/RTX 2080 path rendered Drift with 38 resources (32 compressed), 97232752 upload payload bytes and 46 multilayer draws across six materials. Magione used 63 resources, 125527056 upload bytes and 85 multilayer draws across seven materials. Both report explicit incomplete-shading diagnostics. Grass receives its source detail colour; visible stippling/coplanar artifacts, lighting and full original appearance remain unvalidated.

The multilayer milestone passed 49 GPU-independent tests, nine explicit offscreen GPU tests and four window tests. New fixtures verify complete shader property/sampler retention, missing/ambiguous layer fallbacks, scalar/float2 roles, raw linear-mask mip generation, all four mask weights, gain and coordinate projection. The window test verifies multilayer presentation, camera changes and switching to diagnostic colours. Native/Python material properties and mappings also agree on original fixtures and local Drift/Magione. These tests establish the implemented formula and loading contracts, not original rendered-image parity.

On 2026-10-18, direct BC uploads on Windows/Vulkan/RTX 2080 loaded all 44 referenced Magione resources for all 622 selected draws. Their authored compressed mip payload totalled 99859616 bytes (95.2 MiB), with no resource diagnostics. The frame still has original shader/grass artifacts; source model counts remain 1915816 triangles. Forcing --rgba-textures disabled the device feature, uploaded 36 textures/267310256 payload bytes and reported eight budget fallbacks. The forced RGBA Drift PNG matched the previous software texture frame byte for byte (SHA256 05560595a7047f3f475eeed67fcddc943c9d37a7d21edbc1ed02ff3c9ca6de0e).

The earlier BC implementation passed 45 GPU-independent Rust tests, seven explicit offscreen GPU tests and three window tests. New CPU cases validate exact BC1/2/3 mip payload retention, bounds/truncation, unaligned-base software decode, caching and independent model texture namespaces. The GPU comparison uses BC1, BC2 and BC3 with 12x4 base levels and 6x2, 3x1 and 1x1 authored tails; it checks centre colour/alpha against software decoding and minification into the final mip, with a two-channel-unit tolerance. A device requested without BC explicitly verifies the fallback, and native window smoke also covers --rgba-textures. This is implemented-path evidence, not original-image parity or a performance guarantee.

On 2026-10-18, the native Magione models.ini path assembled both declared KN5 files with 622 selected draws and 1915816 triangles. The 1240 by 900 offscreen Vulkan/RTX 2080 frame uploaded 36 textures for 519 textured draws, with 121 alpha-test and 32 blended draws; 1115583 pixels differed from the clear colour. Eight referenced resources exceeded the shared 256 MiB decoded-texture budget and used diagnostic colours. Road/grass materials remain visibly incomplete. This is composition/readback evidence, not original visual parity.

The earlier composition suite passed 41 GPU-independent tests, six explicit offscreen GPU tests and two explicit native-window tests (KN5 and composed models.ini). New original fixtures check source-aware INI/LUT errors, translation/rebasing/bounds, portable resource confinement, model limits, per-model texture namespaces and a shared source budget. A two-model GPU fixture with identical texture names proves distinct red/green surface pixels. Native/Python contracts also agree on one original INI, seven LUT samples, five config rejection cases and a two-model manifest. A Unix-only fixture additionally checks symlink escape rejection.

On 2026-10-18, native Windows/Vulkan presentation used Bgra8UnormSrgb on the RTX 2080. An original window fixture presented one uncaptured frame and four read-back frames with programmatic resize to 640 by 480, camera changes and a same-camera diffuse toggle that changed surface pixels. Its first 319 by 241 PNG decoded to the expected canonical RGBA clear colour, verifying BGRA conversion. The real Drift window produced a 1240 by 900 perspective surface capture with 25 textures, 254 selected draws and 1150970 triangles; 1115956 pixels differed from clear colour. Refactoring to the persistent shared GPU path retained the previous offscreen Drift PNG byte for byte.

The earlier window implementation had 29 GPU-independent tests, five explicit offscreen GPU tests and one explicit desktop window test. Windows UI automation could not initialise (failed to write kernel assets), so real mouse/keyboard gestures were not independently verified. Camera math, render state and surface presentation evidence must not be presented as full desktop input or original visual parity. Native interactive driving was absent at that earlier window milestone; current driving-window evidence is recorded below.

The subsequent native diffuse path on 2026-10-17 loaded all 25 unique referenced Drift resources (17 BC3, three BC1, four RGB and one luminance), retaining each declared five-level authored mip chain. It uploaded 262586368 decoded RGBA bytes and rendered 254 textured draws, including 78 alpha-test and 24 blended draws, through Vulkan on the RTX 2080 at 1240 by 900. There were no resource-load diagnostics; original shader limitations remain explicit. The frame has 1115882 pixels different from the known clear colour. Grass/material artifacts remain visible and no original-image parity is claimed.

After splitting the implementation into asc-app, asc-kn5, asc-texture and asc-render, 25 GPU-independent Rust tests cover content, camera, DDS and resource resolution. Five explicit GPU tests cover occlusion/readback/PNG, UV orientation, alpha/opacity/blending, depth modes and transparent ordering. Original vectors include both BC3 alpha tables, BC2 explicit alpha, BC1 transparency, cropped blocks, authored compressed/raw mips, raw pitch/masks, truncation/budget rejection, duplicate resources and inverse-transpose normals. The native/Python reader contracts were rechecked on the original fixtures and local Drift/BMW models after reorganisation. This evidence validates the implemented subset rather than the full compatibility target.

On 2026-10-17, the Rust reader agreed with Python on eight original valid fixtures and four original rejection cases, then on local Drift and BMW M3 E30 structural counts, visible mesh/triangle selection and bounds. Drift had 350 nodes, 308 static meshes, 27 materials and 56 texture entries, with 254 selected meshes and 1150970 triangles. The BMW selected 166 static meshes/117597 triangles and explicitly omitted one structurally read skinned mesh. Agreement verifies openASC reader contracts, not original game behavior.

The native wgpu 30.0.1 path rendered Drift at 1240 by 900 through Vulkan on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080, with ROAD camera focus and 1115911 pixels different from the known clear colour (with one-unit channel tolerance). An original two-layer GPU fixture verified depth occlusion independently of submission order, 319-pixel unaligned row readback, exact PNG round-trip and overwrite refusal. Ten GPU-independent Rust tests cover structure, truncated prefixes, nested transforms, visibility/LOD/skinning selection, malformed fields, bounded counts/depth, rebased indices, road focus and camera clip coordinates. These counts and pixel checks establish a real native diagnostic render, not textures, material fidelity, performance guarantees or 1:1 visuals. Only verified CI/backend results should extend the platform record.

On 2026-10-17, the current readers inspected 42 model configurations referencing 295 static model headers in the development installation with no model errors. There were 22 unsupported-section warnings. These are model references, not a count of unique files or fully supported scenes.

The local Drift KN5 was also parsed through its complete supported structure: 350 nodes, 308 static meshes, 27 materials, and 56 indexed embedded textures. The viewer drew 254 visible near-level meshes containing 1150970 triangles. Browser verification checked non-background geometry pixels, WebGL errors, camera changes, top view, mesh focus, and material inspection. The source game file and local screenshots remain outside the repository. This is an approximate preview, not visual parity with Assetto Corsa.

The texture preview loaded 25 unique diffuse resources for all 27 Drift materials: 17 BC3, 3 BC1, 4 RGB, and 1 luminance texture. Both the S3TC-capable and forced software paths uploaded all 25 without JavaScript/WebGL errors. Browser checks verified substantial texture detail, a changed rendered frame when textures were toggled, and top-view rendering. BC2 is covered by original fixtures, not this Drift sample. Three additional original browser pixel fixtures verified that opaque rendering ignores zero texture alpha, alpha test removes transparent pixels, and half-alpha blending produces the expected intermediate colour. Screenshots remain local and are not published.

The ground path assembled 54522 nonvertical/nondegenerate triangles from 56 Drift meshes: 8 ROAD, 39 GRASS and 9 KERB meshes. Six vertical/degenerate triangles and eight WALL meshes were excluded. Two unsupported model-configuration sections remained explicit warnings. One thousand fixed-seed probes placed 0.1 metre above sampled triangle centroids found support within 0.1 metre, with finite upward unit normals. Median query time was approximately 0.072 ms and the 95th percentile approximately 0.195 ms on the development machine; these timings are observations, not real-time guarantees. Independent original fixtures cover analytic ramps, stacked roads, shared edges, opposite winding, transforms, hidden physical meshes, malformed surface definitions, file precedence, misses, and query/budget limits. No tyre or driving compatibility is established by these checks.

The ordinary BMW M3 E30 ACD indexed 45 records without extraction; seven required INI files and the 21-point torque LUT loaded through the vehicle subset. Default tyre compound 2 and an explicit compound 0 both loaded. The model's LF/LR nodes had positive X, RF/RR negative X, and the front pair larger Z than the rear pair, supporting the documented local vehicle axes. Drift provided 35 unambiguous usable markers: 18 PIT, 16 START and one HOTLAP_START. AC_START_3 occurred more than once and remained an error, rather than an arbitrary selection. At AC_PIT_0, all four BMW footprint probes hit ROAD about 0.554 metres below the marker plane; the complete report still has errors because of that separate duplicate start slot. This does not prove chassis equilibrium, correct graphics placement or vehicle dynamics. Original fixtures cover independent checksum/record vectors, packed/unpacked parity, invalid/truncated archives, compound selection, numeric domains, source precedence, rotated spawn axes, parent/mesh aliases, duplicate markers and missing support.

The first-drive browser test rendered BMW M3 E30/Drift using 379 meshes (166 car meshes), 1268075 triangles and 36 uploaded diffuse textures. The driving renderer omitted 41 start/pit/timing helper meshes while retaining their source transforms for inspection. Keyboard checks exercised forward acceleration, left steering, braking, reverse, pause and spawn reset without JavaScript/WebGL errors. Exact speed and path are prototype outcomes, not measured-car validation. Original mathematical fixtures cover forward/reverse steering, mirror symmetry, force-circle bounds, neutral behavior, brake energy dissipation, grade holding, zero-friction motion, missing support and identical fixed-step replays. Local protocol fixtures cover input expiry, paused ticks, nonce/origin checks, replay rejection, invalid commands and in-memory assembly. Selected screenshots now appear on the public website as progress illustrations at the user's request; source game files and detailed local reports remain excluded.

The wall path indexed eight Drift meshes containing 2546 triangles, with no degenerate faces, and derived the BMW body box from its local collider model. Three deterministic straight/left/right input traces each completed 720 steps with wall contacts, no body-proxy penetration and no error pause. The straight trace reached the eight-event motion cap on four steps; the left/right traces did not. Median step time was approximately 0.66 ms and the 95th percentile 2.32 ms in that development run; these are observations, not real-time guarantees. Original fixtures cover thin-wall crossing in both directions, height/edge misses, rotational contacts between clear endpoints, analytic near-tangent skin contact, transformed/degenerate inputs, head-on and glancing response, reverse departure, invalid spawn overlap and 200 randomized impulse energy checks. No original convex collision or full 6DOF parity is established.

All 27 LUT files found under that installation's SDK content examples parsed with the current subset. This is local evidence, not a claim about all original or community content. Validation reports remain under ignored reports/; no source game data is published.

Native DWB geometry validation

The Rust five-link solver is checked against a closed-form parallel-wishbone circle through compression/rebound and return sweeps. Further original fixtures check steering with all five distances preserved, rigid-frame covariance, an analytic Jacobian against independent central differences, singular geometry, an unreachable request inside the numeric command range, invalid inputs and failed-solve immutability. The DWB adapter rejects incomplete DWB and wrong-type STRUT records; STRUT has a separate adapter. A full CLI fixture passes an original INI through the native reader/adapter/solver, checks a closed-form position and unchanged source bytes, and rejects unsupported/invalid/duplicate requests.

Locally, 81 raw-design cases covered BMW M3 E30 rear and Ferrari 458 front/rear: travel from -40 through +40 mm in 10 mm increments, each with -2/0/+2 mm displacement of the inner steering anchor along source X. A separate Python calculation expanded each returned quaternion into a matrix and checked all five distances directly against the source points. Maximum errors were 4.590e-11 m (BMW rear), 1.781e-11 m (Ferrari front), and 1.514e-11 m (Ferrari rear); at most four Newton updates were needed. This proves those source-geometry constraints, not original simulator kinematics. The initial SDK Formula K attempt was rejected because of an unrelated conflict-copy filename; that issue is now resolved by the unpacked index policy. It is not included in this earlier 81-case sweep.

Original-game measurements, mirrored sides, setup camber/toe, source origin/axis interpretation, forces and native wheel animation remain unverified or unimplemented. Reports remain in ignored reports/; no original hardpoints are bundled as fixtures.

Native STRUT geometry validation
